correctness.rationale: Exact original-time polar change gives \(v=r^{-2p}\) with \(\dot v=-2p\lambda v+2pa(\theta)\), so v stays uniformly between positive constants. As the initial angle approaches a source zero of order k, radial equilibration uniformly gives v→a0/λ during the dominant long delay. Direct dt/dtheta=v/g then supplies the precise logarithmic or inverse-power crossing rate; the initial density pushforward gives survival coefficients and moment divergence. All possible cubic multiplicities are at most four because g is a degree-four homogeneous form, and direct factorization Qk yields each order with strict radial contraction. The package standard-library script returned VERIFY_OK as a diagnostic, not a proof.

originality.rationale: The full originating preprint gives polar equations, globally attracting invariant circle, qualitative phase portraits, and finite-zero multiplicities, but no ensemble first-crossing asymptotics in original physical time or exact tail constants. The full 2013 star-node integrability work similarly gives invariant lines/first integrals, not a time-to-ray ensemble. The full Kuehn text studies bottleneck delay as a bifurcation parameter approaches zero, not the late-time distribution of starting points near a true invariant ray. Three closely related published works were checked in full: all concern nonzero angular rotation or periodic-orbit occupation, rather than the actual angular source at zero drift with annular starting data. This is a best-knowledge statement comparison and cannot establish worldwide uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named deterministic intermittency/entrance-time results for invariant-ray ensembles might subsume the pushforward step.

The exponents and multiplicity realizability are largely implications of already-known scalar normal forms and original phase-portrait classes; novelty is limited to the explicit annulus-uniform physical-time survival law and full cubic constants.

value.rationale: The structural question is when a positive area of starting states near a true nonhyperbolic angular separatrix takes arbitrarily long physical time to reach a prescribed observation ray. The theorem answers this with exact heavy-tail constants and a sharp transition between finite and divergent moments. Its complete cubic order spectrum distinguishes four observable regimes that the existing topological classification alone cannot quantify; no claim of a new general scalar slowdown exponent is made.
